title: Reflexive Verbs
summary: The full paradigm behind the set phrases of ¶140: how the reflexive affix -si- conjugates in all three tenses, and how it migrates under negation and under prefixes.

rules.heading: The Reflexive Affix
rules.statement: A **reflexive** verb is marked by the affix **-si-** (infinitive **-tis**): *mokyti* "to teach", *mokytis* "to learn". The affix turns the action back on the doer, or marks a middle meaning that English often renders with a different verb altogether. At A1 the forms were learnt as phrases (¶140); here they are declined in full.

examples.gloss: to teach → to learn / to study
to see → to be visible; to meet (reciprocal)

footnotes: Not every *-tis* verb is literally reflexive: *sektis*, *patikti* (non-reflexive), and *atsiprašyti* show that the affix is also a word-forming device. The conjugation, however, is the same.

rules.heading: The Present of a Reflexive Verb
rules.statement: In the present the affix sits **at the end** of the personal form as **-si** (after a vowel) or **-s** is absorbed into the ending. The first person singular ends in **-ausi / -uosi / -iuosi** according to conjugation; the third person in **-asi / -osi / -isi**. Person is marked as on a non-reflexive verb; only the *-si* is added.

paradigms.caption: mokytis — present (conj. II pattern)
paradigms.footnote: As always, one third-person form serves singular and plural. Further examples: *jaustis → jaučiuosi, jautiesi, jaučiasi*; *praustis → prausiuosi, prausiesi, prausiasi*.

rules.heading: Past and Future Reflexives
rules.statement: In the **past** and the **future** the same affix rides at the end: *mokėsi, mokysis*. The past follows the verb's ordinary type (*-o* or *-ė*); the future keeps the *-s-* marker and adds *-i(s)*. The infinitive is always **-tis**.

examples.gloss: Tomorrow I shall study at home.

rules.heading: Migration under Negation
rules.statement: Under **negation** the affix leaves the end of the word and stands **immediately after *ne-***: *mokausi* but **nesimokau**; *jaučiuosi* but **nesijaučiu**. The personal ending is then the ordinary non-reflexive one. Without this rule a negated reflexive is unrecognisable.

paradigms.caption: Affirmative against negated
paradigms.footnote: The same migration appears in set phrases: *atsiprašau* but *neatsiprašau* is a prefixed case (¶153); plain *nesijaučiu* is the bare pattern.

examples.target: Aš mokausi, bet dar nesimokau rašyti.
examples.gloss: I am learning, but I am not yet learning to write.
Today I do not feel well.
They do not wash in the mornings.

rules.heading: Migration under a Prefix
rules.statement: When the verb already carries a **prefix**, the reflexive affix sits **between the prefix and the stem**: *šypsotis* → *nusišypsoti* → *nusišypsau*; *sakyti* → *atsisakyti* → *atsisakau*. Negation then precedes the whole complex: **nenusišypsau**, **neatsisakau**. The order is always *ne- + prefix + -si- + stem*.

examples.gloss: He did not refuse to help.

rules.heading: What the Affix Can Mean
rules.statement: The same morphology covers several senses, and the dictionary — not the ending — chooses among them. **True reflexive**: the doer acts on himself (*prausiuosi*). **Reciprocal**: each acts on the other (*matomės*, we meet / see each other). **Middle / lexical**: a new verb whose English counterpart is rarely reflexive (*mokytis* learn, *jaustis* feel, *sektis* go well).

examples.gloss: I wash myself with cold water.

rules.heading: Complements of Reflexive Verbs
rules.statement: A reflexive verb may still govern a case. **Mokytis** takes the **genitive** of the subject studied (*mokausi lietuvių kalbos*); **domėtis** and **rūpintis** take the **instrumental** (taught with the unexpected-case verbs of the next section); many true reflexives take no object at all. Do not put an accusative after *mokytis* where English "learn Lithuanian" tempts one to.

examples.note: predicative adjective agreeing with the subject

footnotes: *Mokyti* (non-reflexive) takes an accusative of the person taught and often a genitive of the subject: *mokau vaiką matematikos*.

vocabulary.gloss: to give a smile, to smile (once)

vocabulary.notes: Source of the set phrase atsiprašau.

drills.stem: What is the infinitive reflexive corresponding to **mokyti**?
drills.explanation: The infinitive adds **-tis**: *mokytis*. *mokausi* is already a finite first-person form.

drills.stem: Complete: **Aš ____ lietuvių kalbos.** (I am learning Lithuanian.)
drills.explanation: *mokausi* is 1 sg. present reflexive. *mokau* would mean "I teach"; *moku* "I know how / I pay".

drills.stem: Negate **mokausi**: which form is correct?
drills.explanation: Under negation *-si-* migrates after *ne-*: **nesimokau**. Leaving *-si* at the end (*nemokausi*) is the error the rule exists to prevent.

drills.stem: What is the 3rd-person past of **mokytis**?
drills.explanation: Past reflexive: *mokėsi*. *mokė* is the non-reflexive past; *mokosi* present; *mokysis* future.

drills.stem: In which forms has **-si-** migrated away from the end of the word?
drills.explanation: Negation and prefixes pull *-si-* forward. Only *jaučiuosi* still has the affix at the end.

drills.stem: **Mes dažnai matomės.** What sense of the reflexive is this?
drills.explanation: Reciprocal: each participant is both doer and undergoer. A true reflexive would be one person acting on himself.

drills.stem: Complete: **Mokausi ____.** (I am learning Lithuanian — the language as object.)
drills.explanation: *mokytis* governs the **genitive** of the subject studied. The accusative is what *mokyti* (to teach) or *mokėti* might lead a learner to write, and it is wrong here.

drills.stem: Which statements about prefixed reflexives are **correct**?
options: In *nusišypsau*, -si- stands after the prefix nu-.
The order under negation is ne- + prefix + -si- + stem.
drills.explanation: The wrong third option invents a double migration (*nesi-nu-*). Correct is **nenusišypsau**: *ne-* then *nu-* then *-si-* then the stem.

drills.stem: What is the 1 sg. future of **jaustis**?
drills.explanation: Future stem *jaus-* + 1 sg. + reflexive: **jausiuosi**. *jaučiuosi* is present; *nesijausiu* is the negated future (affix already migrated).

drills.stem: **Prausiuosi** against **mokausi** — same morphology, different meaning type. Which pairing is right?
drills.explanation: *praustis* is washing oneself (true reflexive); *mokytis* is a lexical middle whose English is "learn", not "teach oneself".

drills.stem: In the present paradigm of **mokytis**, how many **distinct** written forms cover all six person/number slots?
drills.explanation: Five: *mokausi, mokaisi, mokosi, mokomės, mokotės*. The third person *mokosi* covers both singular and plural, so six slots but five spellings.

drills.stem: How many times does the letter sequence **si** appear in the correctly negated form of *jaučiuosi* (1 sg. present)?
drills.explanation: **nesijaučiu** contains one *si*, right after *ne-*. The final *-si* of the affirmative has gone; counting two would mean the affix was left at the end as well.

drills.stem: Which of these are **reflexive** infinitives?
drills.explanation: *mokyti* is the non-reflexive "to teach". The *-tis* ending marks the reflexive infinitive.

drills.title: Rytas
drills.passage: Rytą aš keliuosi anksti, prausiuosi ir rengiuosi. Paskui mokausi lietuvių kalbos valandą, bet kartais nesimokau — tada jaučiuosi blogai. Sesuo nusišypso: „Kaip sekasi?“ — klausia ji. „Gerai, tik nesijaučiu žvali,“ — atsakau. Mes matomės vakare. Ji niekada neatsisako padėti, kai prašau.
drills.translation: In the morning I get up early, wash and dress. Afterwards I study Lithuanian for an hour, but sometimes I do not study — then I feel bad. My sister smiles: "How are you getting on?" she asks. "Fine, only I do not feel lively," I answer. We meet in the evening. She never refuses to help when I ask.

questions.stem: Which form in the passage is a **negated** reflexive with migrated *-si-*?
questions.explanation: *nesimokau* shows *ne- + si + stem*. *nusišypso* is prefixed but affirmative.

questions.stem: Which verbs in the passage are **prefixed** reflexives?
questions.explanation: *nu-si-šypso* and *ne-at-si-sako* carry a prefix with *-si-* inside. *keltis* and *praustis* are plain reflexives.

questions.stem: **Mes matomės vakare.** What does the reflexive express here?

How many **finite reflexive verb forms** (affirmative or negated) appear in the passage? Count *keliuosi, prausiuosi, rengiuosi, mokausi, nesimokau, jaučiuosi, nusišypso, sekasi, nesijaučiu, matomės, neatsisako*.
questions.explanation: Eleven finite reflexives as listed. *atsakau*, *klausia*, and *prašau* are not reflexive.

questions.stem: Why is it **lietuvių kalbos** after *mokausi*, not *kalbą*?
options: Because *mokytis* takes a genitive complement of the subject studied.
questions.explanation: ¶155: *mokytis* + genitive. The verb is affirmative here, so negation-genitive is irrelevant.

drills.stem: What is the 1 sg. present of **praustis**?
drills.explanation: Present reflexive ends in **-uosi / -ausi**: *prausiuosi*.

drills.stem: Complete: **Kaip tu ____?** (How do you feel?)
drills.explanation: Second person singular present: *jautiesi*.

drills.stem: The correct negation of **jaučiuosi** is:
drills.explanation: Under negation *-si-* migrates after *ne-*: **nesijaučiu** — ordinary personal ending, no final *-si*.

drills.stem: What is the 3rd-person future of **mokytis**?
drills.explanation: Future keeps the *-s-* marker and adds reflexive *-is*: *mokysis*.

drills.stem: Where does **-si-** sit in **nusišypsojo**?
options: at the end of the word
between the prefix and the stem
drills.explanation: Under a prefix the affix stands **between prefix and stem**: *nu- + -si- + šypsojo*.

drills.stem: Which forms show **-si-** migrated (not sitting at the word end)?
drills.explanation: Negation and prefixes pull *-si-* forward. Only *prausiuosi* still has the affix finally.

drills.stem: Complete: **Mokausi ____.** (I am learning Lithuanian.)
drills.explanation: *Mokytis* takes the **genitive** of the subject studied: *mokausi lietuvių kalbos*.

drills.stem: What is the 1 sg. past of **mokytis**?
drills.explanation: Past 1 sg. reflexive: *mokiausi*. *mokėsi* is third person; *mokausi* is present.

drills.stem: Which sense labels fit?
drills.explanation: *Mokytis* is a lexical middle ('learn'), not reciprocal. Reciprocal needs mutual action (*matomės*).

drills.stem: Negated prefixed form of *nusišypsau* is:
drills.explanation: Order is always *ne- + prefix + -si- + stem*: **nenusišypsau**.

drills.stem: How many times does the letter sequence **si** appear in **nesimokau**?
drills.explanation: One *si*, right after *ne-*. The final *-si* of *mokausi* is gone.

drills.stem: How many **person/number slots** does the present of a reflexive verb such as *mokytis* fill?
drills.explanation: Six. The third-person spelling is shared by singular and plural, but both slots exist.

drills.stem: What is the infinitive of **rengtis**'s non-reflexive pair idea (to dress someone)? Approximate stem:
drills.explanation: Infinitive reflexive **-tis** pairs with non-reflexive **-ti**: *rengti → rengtis*.

drills.stem: Which sentences are correctly formed?
drills.explanation: Negation must migrate: not *mokausi ne* but *nesimokau*. The others follow ¶152–¶153 and the present paradigm.
